adult: This topic asks you to understand and use question words (who, what, where, when, why, how) to form and answer questions.
Sorting words into categories and finding synonyms and antonyms helps us remember them.
It builds on Listening and responding and leads to Asking Questions.
To learn a new word, we say it, find out what it means, use it in a sentence and link it to words we know.
kid: New words help you say more.
Use clues to work out a word.

pool.prompt: What should you do when a sentence doesn't make sense?

choices: Sitting up and holding the pencil softly
Writing as fast as you can
pool.explain: A soft grip and good posture give control.
pool.prompt: What helps your writing stay neat?

choices: Writing on lined paper and starting each letter in the right place
pool.explain: Lines and correct starting points keep letters even.
pool.hint: Apply the idea to this situation.
pool.prompt: A child's letters are all different sizes and drift above the line. What would help most?

pool.explain: It starts with a capital and ends with a question mark.
pool.hint: Capital letter, and it is a question.

choices: Read it back and improve it
pool.explain: Good writers reread and improve their work.
pool.prompt: What should you do after writing a draft?

choices: Varying the sentence openings and adding detail
pool.explain: Different openings and detail make writing interesting.
pool.hint: Apply the idea to this situation.
pool.prompt: A student writes: 'We went to the beach. We went swimming. We went home.' What would improve it most?

choices: A school garden would help us learn science and eat healthily.
pool.explain: A clear opinion with a reason persuades.
pool.hint: Apply the idea to this situation.

mt_6lHBTwQPrS.title: Question Words

visual.caption: Sort each word into its category.

steps: Who: a person. Where: a place. When: a time.
'___ is the party?' asks about time: When.
'___ is your teacher?' asks about a person: Who.
